summary: The sole occurrence confirms existing I.1 erlaubt sein, passen. Place/theme is i dukṯaṯi and -lan marks the affected group or party for whom the place is suitable/permitted. No new lexical sense, box or idiom is needed.

The full context contrasts former status as aġawat with relocating to a suitable place. Thus suitability/admissibility is supported, but formal legal prohibition versus social appropriateness is not independently distinguishable here. The German and inherited gloss are preserved.

96/27: segment haw and final -yo in haw gǧoyazlanyo. Does -yo resume the feminine place/theme, act as a copular/deictic element, or have another function? The feminine noun alone does not prove a feminine finite verb ending in gǧoyaz-.

How should -lan be described in this predicate: affected party, beneficiary, or experiencer? Confirm whether the clause states prohibition or contextual unsuitability; the supplied translation alone does not select between them.
